name: IEC T (toggle) flip-flop
summary: IEC bistable with a 1T toggle input; when T is active, each clock edge changes the stored state.
description: The toggle input T causes the internal state to change to its complement. In IEC form it is labelled 1T when controlled by a C1 clock, or drawn as a single dynamic T input where each transition toggles. A T stage is the basic divide-by-two element in counters and frequency dividers.

Dedicated T flip-flop packages are rare; the function is usually built from a JK with J and K tied high or a D flip-flop with its complemented output fed back. Functional logic drawings, PLC function-block diagrams and FPGA documentation still use the T form because it states the intent clearly.
The symbol does not show how the toggle function is implemented. Where a JK or D device is used, the physical wiring should appear on the detailed schematic.
readingNotes: Read T as change state on each enabled clock.
Check the implementation on the detailed schematic.
drawingChecklist: Label the toggle input as 1T with a C1 clock, or as a dynamic T.
Cross-reference the implementing JK or D device.
distinction: A JK flip-flop provides set, reset, hold and toggle; a T element provides only hold and toggle.
